mainTopic: Liability for offering outside the עזרה, a טמא who eats impure קודש, and the stringencies of slaughtering versus offering up outside
overview: The amud opens with a question: if a pigeon's head has less than a כזית of meat, does the salt stuck to it count toward the כזית? Salt differs from a bone in ways that could matter to both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and the question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא brings two defenses of רבי יוסי הגלילי, who exempts one who slaughters outside and then offers up outside. רבי says the animal was never fit, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the מזבח would not accept it. זעירי and רבה each name a case where these two reasons give different rulings. Then the גמרא explains the dispute about a טמא who eats impure קודש. רבא says they argue only when the meat became impure first, and the question is whether we say מיגו. רב אשי adds that the body's impurity is not clearly more severe than the meat's. A new משנה then compares slaughtering and offering up outside, and the גמרא begins working out which words in the פסוקים teach each of its rules, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does salt help a pigeon head reach a כזית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a pigeon head with less than a כזית of meat, where the salt on it completes the כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pigeon's head that has less than an olive-size of meat, but the salt on it brings it up to an olive-size: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. Does salt stuck to a pigeon's head count toward the כזית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every קרבן is salted, so the salt sits right on the meat. The head alone is too small to make a כזית, and the salt is what would push it over. The question is whether that salt counts, so that one would be liable for offering it outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of a young pigeon brought as a bird offering
An olive-size; the minimum amount for liability
Salt, which is put on every קרבן
Completes it; brings it up to the full amount
What is the law? (opens a question)

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ בֶּן יוֹנָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: The head of a pigeon that does not have an olive-size of meat,
but the salt completes it to an olive-size: what is the law?
phrases.notes: Every קרבן must be salted (ויקרא 2:13), so salt is stuck to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether salt stuck to a pigeon head counts toward the כזית needed for liability.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the known מחלוקת?
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא asks רב אשי whether this question is already covered by the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא from Parzakya said to רב אשי: Isn't this exactly the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזקיא challenges the question itself. He says it isn't new, because it seems to match an argument we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argued whether a bone attached to meat counts toward the כזית. רבא מפרזקיא assumes salt is just like the bone. If so, רבי יוחנן would say it counts and ריש לקיש would say it doesn't, and there is nothing new to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...?
Their argument (מחלוקת)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הַיְינוּ פְּלוּגְתַּיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: Isn't this the argument between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish?
phrases.notes: He means their argument about a bone attached to the meat of a קרבן: does it count toward the כזית?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו הַיְינוּ פְּלוּגְתַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 1 is really a new question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to ask the question at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt joining the meat seems the same as a bone joining the meat. That case is already the subject of a known מחלוקת.

steps.title: The question works for both sides
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the question can be asked even according to רבי יוחנן, and also according to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to רבי יוחנן, and the question can be asked according to ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that this is not simply the same argument. This short line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that salt is different from a bone. Each opinion could go either way about salt. The next two steps explain why for each side.

keyTerms.meaning: The question can be asked; it is still in doubt

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Rabbi Yochanan,
and the question can be asked according to Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְתִיבְּעֵי לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: salt is not the same as a bone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salt is just like a bone, so the known מחלוקת already decides it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Salt differs from a bone, so the question is open even within each opinion.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן might not count salt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן counted a bone because it is the same kind as meat. Salt is not the same kind as a pigeon, so maybe it doesn't count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question for רבי יוחנן: maybe he only said it there about a bone, because a bone is the same kind as meat. But salt is not the same kind as a pigeon, so maybe it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן might not count the salt, even though he counted the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason for joining the bone may be that bone and meat both come from the animal. Salt is a different substance from the bird. So even רבי יוחנן might say salt does not join.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said it up to this point (in that case)
There (in the earlier case)
Bone
Kind, type

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan only said it there
about a bone, since it is the same kind as meat;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֶלַח, דְּלָאו מִינָא דְּבַר יוֹנָה הוּא – לָא.
phrases.english: but salt, which is not the same kind as a pigeon, not.
phrases.notes: The ending "not" means maybe he would not count the salt toward the כזית.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 3's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting רבי יוחנן's ruling to things of the same kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן counts anything attached, including salt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי יוחנן counts only the same kind, like bone with meat, and not salt.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש might count salt
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש did not count a bone because a loose bone need not go on the מזבח. Salt must go on the מזבח even if it falls off, so maybe it does count. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question for ריש לקיש: maybe he only said it there, because if the bone comes off there is no מצוה to put it on the altar. But here, if the salt comes off there is a מצוה to put it on the altar, so maybe he would not say it. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש might count the salt, even though he did not count the bone. Then it gives the other side of the doubt: maybe the cases are the same after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's reason for not joining the bone may be that a bone is not itself part of what goes up on the מזבח. Salt is different: even if it separates, it must still be offered. That makes it more a part of the offering. The closing line, או דלמא לא שנא, keeps the doubt open for both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates, comes off
A מצוה to offer it up on the מזבח
Or perhaps
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: Salt differs from bone in two ways. It is not the same kind as the bird, which might weaken it for רבי יוחנן. It must be offered even when it separates, which might strengthen it for ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הָתָם,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish only said it there,
because if the bone separates from it,
there is no מצוה to offer it up;
but here, where if the salt separates,
there is a מצוה to offer it up, not.
phrases.notes: The "not" here means maybe ריש לקיש would not rule as he did by the bone, so the salt would count.

phrases.english: Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of step 3's answer, then states the opposite side of the doubt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting ריש לקיש's ruling to things that need not be offered on their own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש never counts anything extra, including salt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe ריש לקיש would count salt, since it must be offered even when separate. Or maybe there is no difference.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof was found either way. So it stays uncertain whether salt joins a pigeon head to make a כזית for liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The question about salt completing a כזית on a pigeon head ends as a תיקו, unresolved.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question after both sides of the doubt were laid out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains unresolved whether salt counts toward the כזית of a pigeon head offered outside.

steps.title: Quoting the opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion in the משנה, opening a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי from the משנה to open a new topic. This line sets up the defenses of his opinion that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי הגלילי says that one who slaughters outside and offers up outside is exempt, because he offered something already unfit. The חכמים challenged him: an animal slaughtered inside and then taken out is also unfit, yet one is liable. The משנה did not give his answer, so the גמרא now brings one.

keyTerms.meaning: "And so on." The rest of the quote is in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. It has nothing to do with the salt question that ended in תיקו. The גמרא is going back to a different line of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says, etc.
phrases.notes: He says: if you slaughtered outside and then offered up outside, you are exempt for the offering up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the salt question ended in תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slaughters outside and offers up outside is exempt for the offering up, since the קרבן was already unfit.

steps.title: רבי's defense: the animal once had a moment of being fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי defends רבי יוסי הגלילי. An animal slaughtered inside was fit for a moment, but one slaughtered outside was never fit at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי answered for רבי יוסי הגלילי: You cannot compare the two cases. The animal slaughtered inside and offered outside once had a moment when it was fit. The animal slaughtered outside and offered outside never had a moment of fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the חכמים' challenge to רבי יוסי הגלילי. He shows that their example is different from the case of slaughtering outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said both animals are unfit when offered outside, so both should be treated the same. רבי says no. The one slaughtered inside was fully fit for a moment before it was taken out. The one slaughtered outside was unfit from the very start, so offering it up is not punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: Answered back, gave a defense
Here it means "on behalf of"
Inside the עזרה / outside the עזרה
A time when the קרבן was fit

phrases.aramaic: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי תַּחַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi responded on behalf of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
What about one who slaughters inside and offers up outside?
There, it had a time of fitness.
Will you say the same about one who slaughters outside and offers up outside,
where it never had a time of fitness?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי תַּחַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the opinion quoted in step 7 against the חכמים' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (מה ל־ ... תאמר ב־)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both animals are unfit when offered outside, so both should carry liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an animal that once had a moment of fitness brings liability when it is offered outside.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's defense: the מזבח would accept it
steps.stepSummary: A second defense: an animal slaughtered inside would be accepted by the מזבח if it were put on it, but one slaughtered outside would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון answered for רבי יוסי הגלילי: The animal slaughtered inside and offered outside is one that the holiness of the מזבח would accept. The animal slaughtered outside is one that the holiness of the מזבח would not accept.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives another way to defend רבי יוסי הגלילי against the same challenge. He uses a different reason to tell the two cases apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is not whether the animal was once fit. The test is whether the מזבח would hold on to it if it were placed there. An animal that became unfit inside the עזרה would stay on the מזבח. An animal slaughtered outside would be taken down, so offering it up is not punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the מזבח accepts it, so if it went up it is not taken down

phrases.aramaic: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן תַּחַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, responded on behalf of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
What about one who slaughters inside and offers up outside?
There, the holiness of the altar accepts it.
phrases.notes: He means that if it were put on the מזבח, it would stay there and not be taken down.

phrases.english: Will you say the same about one who slaughters outside,
where the holiness of the altar does not accept it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן תַּחַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different defense in place of רבי's defense from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases with a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both animals are unfit when offered outside, so both should carry liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability for offering outside applies only to an animal the מזבח would accept.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two defenses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where רבי's defense and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's defense would give different answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two defenses ever lead to a different ruling. This question sets up זעירי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both defenses exempt one who slaughters outside. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the two reasons applies, so the rulings would differ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two defenses from steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two defenses lead to different rulings.

steps.title: זעירי: the difference is an animal slaughtered at night
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says the two defenses differ about an animal slaughtered at night inside the עזרה and then offered up outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: Slaughtering at night is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי answers the question. He names one case, an animal slaughtered at night, where the two defenses give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered at night was never fit, so by רבי's reason one who offers it up outside would be exempt. But a night slaughter done inside is a problem that happened in holy space, and if it goes on the מזבח it is not taken down. So by רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reason, one who offers it up outside would be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן at night, which makes it unfit
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Two defenses of רבי יוסי הגלילי: רבי asks "was it ever fit?" and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון asks "would the מזבח accept it?" An animal slaughtered at night was never fit, but the מזבח would accept it. So the two defenses give different rulings for it.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
Slaughtering at night is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering at night inside the עזרה, and then offering it up outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי שְׁחִיטַת לַיְלָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Night slaughter inside, then offering up outside: exempt according to רבי (never fit), liable according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון (the מזבח would accept it).

steps.title: רבה: The difference is blood collected in a כלי חול
steps.stepSummary: רבה offers a different case from זעירי's for where the two defenses would give different results: the blood was collected in a כלי חול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The difference between them is a case where the blood was collected in a non-sacred vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second answer to the question from Step 10. He offers a different case from זעירי's that shows how the two defenses of רבי יוסי הגלילי lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was slaughtered properly inside the עזרה, but its blood was collected in an ordinary vessel, which disqualifies it. Using רבי's test of whether it was ever fit, the animal counts as disqualified from the start, so a person who then offers it outside is פטור. Using רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's test, this is a disqualification that happened inside the holy area, so the מזבח would accept it, and the person is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving or collecting the animal's blood in a vessel, one of the main services of a קרבן.
An ordinary vessel that was never made holy for use in the בית המקדש.

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not arguing with the rule from Steps 8 and 9. He only offers a different example from זעירי's of where the two defenses would split.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
Collection of the blood in a non-sacred vessel
phrases.notes: Picture the animal slaughtered properly inside, with its blood caught in an ordinary bowl, and then the animal offered up outside.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: קַבָּלָה בִּכְלִי חוֹל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to זעירי's answer in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which practical case do רבי's defense and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's defense lead to different results?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A case where the blood was collected in a non-sacred vessel and the animal was then offered up outside.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about an impure person who ate sacrificial meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a טמא who eats קודש that is either pure or impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: An impure person who ate sacrificial meat, whether it was impure or pure, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of a טמא who eats קדשים. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן hold that a טמא is חייב כרת for eating קודש even if the meat was already impure. רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts him when the meat was impure. The רבנן answered him that even pure meat becomes impure as soon as the טמא touches it.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is ritually impure.
Sacrificial meat that has been made holy.

phrases.english: An impure person who ate, whether sacrificial meat, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line continues: 'whether impure sacrificial meat or pure sacrificial meat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל בֵּין קוֹדֶשׁ כּוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The discussion about offering sacrifices outside is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא who eats קודש, whether it is pure or impure, is liable. רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees in the case of impure meat.

steps.title: The רבנן's argument looks too strong to answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the רבנן's argument seems correct, so it is hard to see why רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן are arguing well against רבי יוסי הגלילי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. The רבנן's point seems to leave him no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן argued that a טמא always makes the meat impure the moment he touches it, before he eats it. If eating impure meat were פטור, nobody could ever be חייב for eating pure meat. That seems to make no sense, so how can רבי יוסי הגלילי hold his view?

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are saying well': their argument seems correct.

phrases.english: The Rabbis are saying well to him,
to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's view in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that a טמא who eats impure קודש is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טמא always makes the meat impure by touching it. So his view would mean nobody is ever חייב, which cannot be right.

steps.title: רבא: When the person became impure first, everyone agrees he is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins to define the dispute. If the person became impure before the meat did, everyone agrees he is חייב, because the כרת prohibition of his body's impurity already applied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whenever the person's body became impure first and only afterward the meat became impure, everyone agrees that he is liable, because impurity of the body carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to answer the challenge by narrowing the dispute. He first sets out the case where everyone agrees, which prepares the way for showing where רבי יוסי הגלילי actually disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. If the person became impure while the meat was still pure, the serious כרת prohibition already applied to him, and it does not go away when the meat later becomes impure. This answers the רבנן's argument: the case they described, where the person touches pure meat, is one where even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the person's own body.
Spiritual 'cutting off': the punishment for a טמא who eats קדשים on purpose.
'Everyone agrees': all opinions agree in this case.
'Because': introduces the reason.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute is only about the case where the meat became impure before the person did. This keeps רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from being knocked down by the רבנן's argument.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Wherever he became impure with impurity of the body
and afterward the meat became impure,
everyone agrees that he is liable,
because impurity of the body carries karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּנִטְמָא טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins to answer the challenge in Step 14 by limiting the scope of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute to a specific case (based on which became impure first).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts every טמא who eats impure meat, which would make liability impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the person became impure before the meat did, all agree he is חייב. The dispute must be about a different order of events.

steps.title: The real dispute: the meat became impure first
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the argument is only when the meat became impure before the person. The רבנן use מיגו to say the person's impurity still takes effect, and רבי יוסי הגלילי does not use מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is when the meat became impure first and then the person became impure. The רבנן hold that we say מיגו, and רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that we do not say מיגו.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the answer he began in step 15. He tells us exactly which case the two sides argue about and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a second prohibition cannot take hold of something that is already forbidden. Once the meat became impure, no one may eat it, so the question is whether the person's later impurity can add its own prohibition. The רבנן say yes because of מיגו: his impurity forbids all קודש to him, pure and impure alike, so it reaches this meat too. רבי יוסי הגלילי does not accept that reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they argue; the case the dispute is really about
Impurity of the קודש meat itself
"Since": since the prohibition reaches other things, it also reaches this one
We say; we accept this line of reasoning

steps.confusionAlert: Here מיגו does not mean the familiar court argument ("he could have made a better claim"). It means that a prohibition which covers more things also takes hold of this item.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact case under dispute. The next two steps test whether רבי יוסי הגלילי's view still makes sense.

phrases.english: Where they argue
is when the meat became impure
and afterward the body became impure.
phrases.notes: "The body" means the person who eats the meat.

phrases.english: For the רבנן hold we say "since",
and רבי יוסי הגלילי holds
we do not say "since."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from step 15 by giving the case where they do argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the dispute to one case and names the reasoning behind each side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי יוסי הגלילי disagreed with obvious reasoning in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only when the meat became impure first, and the dispute depends on whether we accept מיגו.

steps.title: Even without מיגו, the more severe prohibition should take effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי: even if we don't use מיגו, the person's impurity is more severe, so it should still take hold on top of the meat's impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי יוסי: fine, we don't say מיגו. But let the impurity of the body, which is more severe, come and take effect on top of the meat's impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against רבי יוסי הגלילי's side. It uses a different reason why the person's impurity should still take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is another known reason a second prohibition can take hold: if it is more severe than the first one. The person's impurity carries כרת, while eating impure meat is a lighter prohibition. So even without מיגו, the heavier prohibition should still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; fine, let's accept that
Let it come
Severe; more serious
Let it take effect

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי:
granted that we do not say "since";
let the impurity of the body, which is more severe, come
and take effect on top of the impurity of the meat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי נְהִי דְּמִיגּוֹ לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי הגלילי's side of the dispute as just defined.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that the person is not חייב when the meat became impure first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A more severe prohibition can take hold on an existing one. The body's impurity (כרת) is more severe than the meat's impurity, so it should apply even without מיגו.

steps.title: Maybe the meat's impurity is the more severe one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that we cannot be sure the body's impurity is more severe. The meat's impurity is more severe in one way: it can never be purified in a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How do we know that the body's impurity is more severe? Perhaps the meat's impurity is more severe, since it has no purification in a מקוה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי יוסי הגלילי. He questions the assumption that the person's impurity is the heavier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who became טמא can go to the מקוה and become pure, but impure קודש meat stays impure forever. So each prohibition is heavier in its own way, and neither one is clearly more severe overall. Without a clear "more severe" prohibition, רבי יוסי הגלילי can hold that the body's impurity does not take hold on the already-impure meat.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? How is it clear?
Perhaps; maybe it is the other way
Since; for the reason that
Becoming pure by immersing in a ritual bath

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן make the person חייב through מיגו. רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects מיגו. רב אשי adds that, for רבי יוסי הגלילי, the body's impurity is not clearly more severe, because impure meat can never become pure.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
From where do we know that the impurity of the body is more severe?
Perhaps the impurity of the meat is more severe,
since it has no purification in a ritual bath!
phrases.notes: A טמא person can immerse and become pure, but impure קודש meat stays impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי מִמַּאי דְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by challenging its assumption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that one prohibition is clearly more severe
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The body's impurity, which carries כרת, is clearly the more severe prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The meat's impurity is more severe in one way, since it can never be purified. So the body's impurity cannot take hold for being more severe.

steps.title: Each act has its own stringency
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with a general rule: slaughtering outside is stricter than offering up outside in one way, and offering up is stricter than slaughtering in another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There is a stricter side to slaughtering than to offering up, and a stricter side to offering up than to slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a headline: each of the two outside acts, שחיטה and העלאה, is stricter in some way. This line sets up the details that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both acts are forbidden outside the עזרה, but their rules are not identical. The משנה promises one case where שחיטה is stricter and one where העלאה is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא will discuss
A stringency, a stricter side
Slaughtering (here, of an offering outside the עזרה)
Offering up the parts of an offering (here, outside the עזרה)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is a stringency in slaughtering over offering up,
and in offering up over slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּשְּׁחִיטָה מִבָּעֲלִיָּיה, וּבָעֲלִיָּיה מִבַּשְּׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the impure person ended in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטת חוץ and העלאת חוץ each have a stringency the other lacks.

steps.title: Slaughtering for an ordinary purpose
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering is stricter because a person who slaughters an offering outside for an ordinary purpose is חייב, while a person who offers it up outside for an ordinary purpose is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stricter side of slaughtering: one who slaughters for an ordinary purpose is liable, but one who offers up for an ordinary purpose is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the first detail: the case where slaughtering is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person does the act for a הדיוט purpose and not for ה׳, slaughtering outside still makes him חייב. Offering up outside for a הדיוט purpose does not.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary, non-sacred purpose (not for ה׳)
Liable, guilty
Exempt, not liable

phrases.english: The stringency in slaughtering:
that one who slaughters for an ordinary purpose is liable,
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering the offering for a plain, everyday reason, not for ה׳.

phrases.english: but one who offers up for an ordinary purpose is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּשְּׁחִיטָה שֶׁהַשּׁוֹחֵט לַהֶדְיוֹט חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the headline from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering outside for a הדיוט purpose makes one חייב; offering up outside for a הדיוט purpose is פטור.

steps.title: Two people doing the act together
steps.stepSummary: Offering up is stricter because two people who slaughter together are פטור, while two people who offer up a limb together are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stricter side of offering up: two people who held a knife and slaughtered are exempt; if they held a limb and offered it up, they are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second detail: the case where offering up is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people share one act of slaughtering outside, both are פטור. When two people share one act of offering up outside, both are חייב. The משנה states this without giving a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people
A knife
A limb or part of the offering

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה is stricter for a הדיוט purpose; העלאה is stricter when two people do it together.

phrases.english: The stringency in offering up:
two who held a knife and slaughtered are exempt;
if they held a limb and offered it up, they are liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בָּעֲלִיָּיה שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָחֲזוּ בְּסַכִּין וְשָׁחֲטוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second half of the headline from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two who slaughter together outside are פטור; two who offer up together outside are חייב.

steps.title: Offering up several times
steps.stepSummary: If someone offers up parts of an offering outside several separate times, רבי שמעון says he is חייב for each one, and רבי יוסי says he is חייב only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he offered up, then offered up again, and again, he is liable for each offering up; these are the words of רבי שמעון. רבי יוסי says: he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dispute: does each separate offering-up outside create its own liability?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון counts every act of offering up as a separate sin, so he brings a separate חטאת for each. רבי יוסי says the person is חייב only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back and did it again
Each act of offering up
A sin offering, brought for a sin done by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: This is about a person who sins by mistake. 'חייב' here means he must bring a חטאת, so the argument is about how many חטאות he brings.

phrases.english: If he offered up, then went back and offered up,
phrases.notes: Each time he offers up different parts of the offering, by mistake, and as a separate act.

phrases.english: and again offered up,
he is liable for each act of offering up.
These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he is liable only once.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶעֱלָה חָזַר וְהֶעֱלָה וְחָזַר וְהֶעֱלָה חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל עֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from comparing שחיטה and העלאה to a new dispute about repeated העלאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: a separate liability for each offering-up. רבי יוסי: only one liability.

steps.title: Must it be on an altar?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a person is חייב only if he offers up on top of an altar. רבי שמעון disagrees and says he is חייב even if he offers it on a rock or a stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is liable only once he offers it up on top of an altar. רבי שמעון says: even if he offered it up on a rock or on a stone, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second dispute: does offering up outside count only when it is done on an altar?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion is still רבי יוסי, who spoke at the end of the previous step. He says the person is חייב only if he offers on top of a מזבח built outside. רבי שמעון makes the person חייב even for offering on a plain rock or stone that is not an altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The top of an altar
A rock
A stone

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון is the stricter one in both disputes: there is liability for each offering-up, and even offering on a rock counts.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: And he is liable only once he offers it up on top of an altar.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֶעֱלָה עַל הַסֶּלַע אוֹ עַל הָאֶבֶן – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: even if he offered it up on a rock or on a stone, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second dispute between the same תנאים about the requirements for liability for העלאת חוץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: liability only for offering on top of an altar. רבי שמעון: liability even on a rock or stone.

steps.title: Why is offering up for an ordinary purpose exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה says that one who offers up outside for an ordinary purpose is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about someone who offers up outside for an ordinary purpose, that he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the first ruling of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said offering up outside לְהֶדְיוֹט (for an ordinary purpose) is פטור. The גמרא wants to know what makes this case different, especially since slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind a distinction
One who offers up a sacrifice on an altar
An ordinary, non-sacred purpose (not for ה׳)
Exempt from punishment

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about one who offers up for an ordinary purpose, that he is exempt?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה in Step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הַמַּעֲלֶה לְהֶדְיוֹט דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the ruling in Step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for exempting one who offers up for an ordinary purpose

steps.title: The word 'to ה׳' exempts offering up for an ordinary purpose
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק about offering up says לה׳, so you are only liable when offering up for ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: "to ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The פסוק about offering up outside says לה׳, so liability applies only when it is done for ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לה׳ limits the איסור to offering up for the sake of ה׳. If someone offers up for an ordinary purpose, he falls outside the פסוק and is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (in a פסוק)
To ה׳

phrases.english: As it is written: "to ה׳."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:9

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word לה׳ limits liability for offering up to cases done for ה׳

steps.title: But the slaughtering verse also says 'to ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק about slaughtering also says לה׳, yet slaughtering for an ordinary purpose is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding slaughtering, isn't it also written "to ה׳"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If לה׳ exempts an ordinary purpose by offering up, it should do the same by slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said שחיטה for an ordinary purpose is חייב. But the שחיטה פסוק also has the word לה׳. So why doesn't it exempt there too?

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering
Isn't it written? Points out a פסוק to raise a challenge
Also

phrases.english: With slaughtering also,
isn't it written "to ה׳"?!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשְּׁחִיטָה נָמֵי הָכְתִיב לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of לה׳ to exempt an ordinary purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by שחיטה, where an ordinary purpose is still חייב

steps.title: Slaughtering is different because of 'any man'
steps.stepSummary: Answer: by שחיטה the פסוק adds איש איש, a doubled word that includes even slaughtering for an ordinary purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since the verse says: "Any man [איש איש]."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שחיטה is different. The doubled phrase איש איש widens the law to include slaughtering for an ordinary purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word works as an extra inclusion. It overrides the limit of לה׳ by שחיטה, so slaughtering for an ordinary purpose stays חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Because the פסוק says
Any man (literally 'a man, a man'); the doubling is read as including more

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means slaughtering.

phrases.english: since the verse says: "Any man [איש איש]."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:3

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאָמַר קְרָא אִישׁ אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra word in the שחיטה פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לה׳ should exempt an ordinary purpose by שחיטה too
steps.terutzMaskana: איש איש by שחיטה includes even an ordinary purpose

steps.title: But offering up also says 'any man'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק about offering up also says איש איש, so it should also include an ordinary purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding offering up, it is also written: "Any man [איש איש]"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. The same doubled phrase appears by העלאה, so why doesn't it make that case חייב too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If איש איש includes an ordinary purpose by שחיטה, it should do the same by העלאה. Then the משנה's פטור for offering up for an ordinary purpose would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, in the case of
Offering up on an altar

phrases.english: Regarding offering up also
it is written: "Any man [איש איש]"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי הַעֲלָאָה נָמֵי כְּתִיב אִישׁ אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of איש איש to include an ordinary purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase appears by העלאה, where the משנה rules פטור

steps.title: By offering up, 'any man' teaches that two people are liable
steps.stepSummary: Answer: by העלאה, איש איש is used for a different lesson, that two people who offer up a limb together are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is needed to teach that two people who offered up a limb together are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that איש איש by העלאה is already used up for another lesson. It teaches that two people who offer up a limb together are both חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the extra phrase is busy teaching about two people, it cannot also include an ordinary purpose. This also gives the source for Step 21, where two who offer up together are חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another lesson)
A limb of the animal
They are liable

phrases.english: It is needed
phrases.notes: This means the phrase איש איש by offering up is used for a different lesson.

phrases.english: for two who offered up a limb – that they are liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהֶעֱלוּ בְּאֵבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is needed for a different lesson

steps.title: Then by slaughtering, two people should also be liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if so, איש איש by שחיטה should also teach that two who slaughter together are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too it should be needed for two who held a knife and slaughtered together, that they are liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. If איש איש teaches 'two are liable' by offering up, it should teach the same thing by slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That would go against the משנה in Step 21, which says two who slaughter together are פטור. It would also leave no extra phrase to include an ordinary purpose by שחיטה.

steps.title: Slaughtering says 'that man', meaning one and not two
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the שחיטה פסוק says ההוא (that man), which means only one person acting alone, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since the verse says "that" man: one, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that by שחיטה another word blocks the idea of two being liable. The word ההוא is singular, so only one person alone is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ההוא already excludes two slaughterers, איש איש by שחיטה cannot be teaching that two are liable. So it is free to include slaughtering for an ordinary purpose.

steps.title: But offering up also says 'that man'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק about offering up also says ההוא, so two people should be פטור there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, regarding offering up too, isn't it written "that"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more challenge. The word ההוא also appears by העלאה, so it should exclude two people there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ההוא excludes two people by העלאה, then איש איש there is no longer needed for two people. Then it could include an ordinary purpose, against the משנה. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the three expressions straight. לה׳ limits to ה׳‎, איש איש includes more, and ההוא excludes two people. The question each time is which word in which פסוק is used for which lesson.
